bounds: SentenceBoundary
Diversification means spreading investments instead of depending on one company or one asset.
SentenceBoundary
It can reduce the damage caused by one investment performing badly, but it cannot guarantee that losses will not occur.
SentenceBoundary
Startup investments are especially uncertain, and several companies may face similar risks, such as a weak economy or limited access to funding.
SentenceBoundary
Consider a simple fictional illustration: someone puts $1,000 into one startup and that company fails, losing the full $1,000.
SentenceBoundary
Another person divides $1,000 equally across ten unrelated startups.
SentenceBoundary
If one fails completely and the other nine merely return the original $100 each, the second person would have $900, before fees and any tax effects.
SentenceBoundary
Real outcomes can be better or worse, and the companies may not be truly independent.
SentenceBoundary
Diversification does not make an unsuitable investment suitable.
SentenceBoundary
Think about your overall finances, emergency savings, time horizon, and concentration across industries and companies.
SentenceBoundary
Do not confuse owning several startup securities with a balanced financial plan.
